clues.text: A sheepherder from Tekoa, he saw visions about Israel two years before the earthquake.
He told a priest at Bethel he was no prophet's son, but a herdsman who tended sycamore-fig trees.
The Lord asked this prophet what he saw, and he answered that it was a plumb line.
God showed this prophet a basket of summer fruit, meaning the end had come for Israel.
Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent word to King Jeroboam that this man had conspired against him.
Amaziah told this seer to flee to Judah, earn his bread there, and never prophesy at Bethel again.
He brought the LORD's judgment on Damascus for three transgressions, even four, for threshing Gilead with iron sledges.
